verdicts.reason: Span confirmed: `return value as SourceTransport;` at src/config.ts:198, live production code in sourceTransportOrUndefined (SourceTransport = "direct"|"ssh"). But the cast does not defeat a contract: its only consumer (readSourceConfigInput) feeds an object that is immediately Zod-validated — configSchema/sourceConfigSchema include `sourceTransport: z.enum(["direct","ssh"])` (line 93) and loadConfig/loadSourceConfig call safeParse and throw ConfigValidationError on any non-union value (lines 240,272). So a bogus string can never survive; the cast is a pre-safeParse staging shape, a safe-but-unexplained cast, exactly the false-positive class the rubric says to reject. No subtype-substitution (LSP) relationship is involved either.

Line 128 of src/discovery/discover.ts contains exactly `const parsed = JSON.parse(text) as Partial<SourceFixture>;` as live production code in parseSourceFixture. JSON.parse returns any; the cast asserts a shape the value is not guaranteed to have — the canonical unchecked-JSON.parse case the rule targets. Only Array.isArray is checked (line 130), yet line 132 returns parsed.candidates typed as readonly SourceCandidateFixture[] (elements with required filename/url) without validating element shape, and the cast carries no comment explaining why it is safe (violating shared-ts-standards §B "no unexplained as casts"). Confidence is medium, not high, because toReplayCandidate re-validates each element downstream, so the contract defeat does not actually cause a runtime bug — but the cast site itself still asserts an unguaranteed shape, matching the rule.

The span exists verbatim at lines 59-61, but the finding misclassifies it. golden-fixtures.ts is test-support code — imported ONLY by golden-*.integration.test.ts, carries the `fixtures` marker (line 12) that depcruise excludes from production rules — yet it's filed `lane production` 🔴. The real cited rule is ts-standards "No unexplained `as` casts" (a typing-hygiene/style rule, at most 🟡 on production), not any LSP/Liskov contract: JSON.parse returns `any`, so `as GoldenManifest` is not a subtype-substitution violation, and the rule id `lsp-no-as-contract-defeat` does not exist in the skill set. Re-grading this as a 🔴 production LSP-contract-defeat invents a stricter rule and wrong lane; the manifest is also a human-authored, repo-committed corpus whose shape and throw semantics are documented in the module docblock (lines 50-57), so the cast is not the untrusted-input contract defeat claimed.

Span exists verbatim at lines 63-65 as live production code. But the cited rule (correctness → Contract compliance/LSP, per backend-ts standards §"Contract compliance (LSP)") targets an `as`-cast that forces a value to satisfy a declared contract/interface/factory it does not fulfill. Here no contract is implemented: `match.groups` is cast to a keyed Record after the regex (lines 54-57) matched all six mandatory named groups (`\d{...}`, none optional) AND after the `if (match?.groups === undefined) return undefined` guard — so the value IS guaranteed to have exactly that shape. This is a type-SAFE narrowing cast, not a contract defeat (unlike an unchecked JSON.parse). At most it's an "unexplained `as` cast" lacking a comment — a different rule (ts-standards §Type declarations), not the LSP/contract rule cited. False positive against the cited rule.

Line 40 `const checksum = calculateSha256(bytes)` is present and live. But calculateSha256 (checksum.ts) is `createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex")` — a pure CPU hash that performs NO I/O, so it does not match the rule's literal "blocking I/O" / "no sync fs reads" target, nor the finding's std-label. The only clause it could touch is "no sync hashing of large input on a hot path," which is qualified by BOTH large-input AND hot-path; here it is one hash per fetched replay in an ingestion-staging step (not a shared request hot path) with no evidence of large input. Rule base severity is 🟠 (🔴 only when it stalls a hot/shared path), so the 🔴 grade is also unjustified. False positive.

falsePositives.reason: The quoted docblock exists at lines 1-3, but the file is scripts/capture-golden-fixtures.ts — a human-run capture utility the skill (and the file's own header, lines 18-20) explicitly places OUTSIDE tsconfig/knip/depcruise scope and the coverage gate, never run by the executor. The actual rule co-locates UNIT tests with source (x.ts→x.test.ts) and gates only "reachable-source" coverage; it does not mandate a paired test for deliberately out-of-scope, non-reachable scripts. Flagging this invents a universal "every .ts needs a test" rule the skill never states. The evidence quoted is also a JSDoc comment, not live testable code.

The span at run-once.ts:104-108 exists and is live production code, but it is resource CONSTRUCTION (`createStoreRawResources(deps, config, true)`), not a shutdown path. The cited rule targets a SIGTERM/SIGINT handler that drains in-flight work and tears down — fetcher form: "finish-or-checkpoint the current item, then teardown." run-once is a one-shot CLI command that runs one cycle and sets process.exitCode; the daemon is watch.ts, which calls the identical resource factory then wires createShutdownSeam() (SIGTERM/SIGINT) + try/finally dispose — i.e., the rule IS satisfied where it applies. Aiming graceful-shutdown at a construction call in a short-lived command is not a violation of that rule as written; a never-closed pool would be the separate §AB resource-lifecycle rule, not graceful-shutdown. False positive.

The throw at src/config.ts:26 is present, but it does NOT violate typed-errors-only as written. The rule scopes itself to "ingest logic / business logic" whose errors propagate to the CLI exit-code boundary (std §B, conv Phase 1 item 3 + severity row "Raw Error from ingest logic"). This throw lives inside the `booleanFromEnvironment` Zod `.transform()` callback in the config-validation schema — not ingest logic. Both schemas are consumed only via `.safeParse` (lines 240, 272), so Zod catches the thrown Error and turns it into a ZodError issue, which loadConfig/loadSourceConfig then wrap into the typed `ConfigValidationError` (an AppError). This is exactly the §C-mandated "safeParse + a typed error; a raw ZodError never escapes" flow — the raw Error never propagates out. Idiomatic Zod custom-validation throw; the finding pattern-matched the literal `throw new Error` text and ignored both the rule's scope and the safeParse boundary.

Span confirmed at config.ts:5 (`import type { SourceTransport } from "./discovery/types.js"`). But it does not violate band-wrong-placement as written. (a) That rule targets a FILE sitting in the wrong band; config.ts is in its CORRECT band — the §A table lists `config.ts` explicitly under Cross-cutting "Holds today." The real concern here is an upward import (Cross-cutting → Capability), which is fence #1 (dependency-direction), a different rule the finding mislabels. (b) The reviewer skill (solidstats-fetcher-ts-code-review SKILL.md L116-126) explicitly SUSPENDS band-membership, layer-placement, dependency-direction, and module-layout findings: the five-band architecture is PROPOSED/PENDING, the code "still predates the refactor," and the depcruise fences/layer checks only switch on once the trio is wired into the repo. No band-placement finding may be raised today. False positive.

The span at line 61 is the real test `test("MD: a full rate-limited window...")`, which starts with capital "M". But §D of the shared testing standards (line 111-112) REQUIRES a test name to "start with a capital letter when it begins with ordinary descriptive text" — capitalization is mandated, not forbidden. The rule label `test-naming-does-not-start-capital` inverts the actual rule. The name complies with §D (and the "MD" prefix is also fine), so the pattern this finding claims does not match.

Span is present verbatim at line 8, and it is live production code. But §A #5 targets a *cross-band upward* type import (the worked example: `RunSummary` in `run/`-Orchestration imported upward by `evidence/`-Adapter). Here both `storage/` and `staging/` are the SAME band (Capability, SKILL.md line 86), and `RawReplayStorageEvidence` is `storage/`'s own output contract that `staging/` consumes downstream (storage→staging data-flow), not an upward reach. No fence forbids capability-to-capability type imports. The finding stretches a cross-band upward rule onto a legitimate same-band sibling import.

The import exists at staging/types.ts:1 as quoted. But rule #5 (cross-band-type-in-types-dir) targets a cross-BAND contract imported UPWARD by a lower band (its sole example: adapter evidence/ reaching up into orchestration run/ for RunSummary — "a layer violation"). Per the §A table, staging/ and storage/ are BOTH the Capability band, so this is a horizontal sibling-capability import of storage's own output type (RawReplayStorageEvidence, defined and produced in storage/), not an upward cross-band leak. No band is reached into upward, no boundary fence forbids it, and the layer-violation harm the rule exists to prevent is absent. The finding over-extends an upward-import rule to safe peer-capability type reuse.

Line 11 does contain the quoted live `import type { ReplayCandidate }` in production code, but it does not violate the cited rule. §A's band table and its enforceable fences (#1–#8) never forbid the storage band from consuming discovery's output payload type. `ReplayCandidate` is the natural downstream pipeline contract (discover → fetch → store); `storeRawReplay`/storage `types.ts` are all built to consume it. Fence #6 constrains the OPPOSITE direction (`discovery/` must not import `storage/`), and the §A-derived depcruise preset has only `no-commands-to-storage-direct` — nothing against storage→discovery. The one upward-import smell §A actually names is `evidence/ → run/` (RunSummary), a different file/rule (adjustment-5 "cross-band contracts live in types/", explicitly gated on the not-yet-done migration). Flagging this type-only sibling import as a "defined responsibility"/band-placement violation invents a stricter rule than the one written.

Quoted import is present at line 9 (a type-only import of ReplayCandidate from ../discovery/types.js). But the finding is invalid: (1) the code-review skill explicitly SUSPENDS this finding class — "do NOT raise band-membership, layer-placement, dependency-direction, or module-layout findings" until §A (PROPOSED/pending sign-off) ships its depcruise fences. (2) On the merits the band table is not violated: discovery/ and storage/ are BOTH in the Capability band, so this is a same-band peer import, not an upper/lower direction violation (fence #1 downward-only N/A). The only directional fence between them, #6, forbids discovery→storage — the opposite direction; nothing forbids storage→discovery. ReplayCandidate is the pipeline-wide candidate contract imported from discovery/types.js by ~every band (run/, commands/, config, contract-check/, check/, types/), i.e. a de-facto cross-band contract. False positive.
